sentences.text:
The present appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/claimant, challenging the award dated 15.07.2016, passed by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sardarpur, District Dhar in Claim Case No.13/2015, whereby the learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim case and awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.5,63,000/-
along with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum.

sentences.text: 2. The factual matrix of the case is that on 09.10.2013, at around 6:30 P.M. deceased met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1.
As a result of which deceased sustained grievous injuries and died during treatment.
Thereafter, dependents/claimants of the deceased filed a claim petition under Section 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.11,00,000/- along with interest.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3450 2 MA-2292-2016 3.
Learned claims Tribunal found that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 which was insured with respondent No.3 on the fateful day.
Thus, learned MACT after appreciating the evidence on record partly allowed the claim petition and awarded a total sum of Rs.5,63,000/- as against the claim of Rs.11,00,000/-.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that learned claims tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.3000/- per month.

He further submits that learned tribunal has erred in not awarding single penny in the head of future prospects and loss of consortium and the tribunal has also not properly calculated the award in the head of funeral expenses and the loss of estate.

sentences.text: He prays for enhancement of the award amount.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent submitted that the finding arrived at by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not call for interference in this appeal by this Court in this appeal.
He further submits that income which has been pleaded in the appeal is Rs.4,500/- and thus, deceased's income is not entitled for enhancement.
6. It is not in dispute that respondent No.1 was responsible for causing the accident on the fateful day, the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3.
The only question for determination in this appeal is whether the amount awarded by the Tribunal requires modification or not?
7. I have heard the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3450 3 MA-2292-2016 8.
Upon perusal of the record and material available on record, this Court is of the opinion that the learned tribunal has assessed lower side income of the deceased.

The deceased at the time of accident was 30 years and as per the revised guidelines of the M.P. State Legal Service authority , at the time of accident, the monthly income of unskilled labour was Rs.5520/- per month, whereas the learned tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.3000/- per month only.
Therefore, considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, the income of the deceased would be considered as Rs.5520/- instead of Rs.3000/- per month.

Therefore, after applying the law laid down in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 4 ACJ 270 Sarla & Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Others, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 the claimant is entitled to get the compensation as under:
Loss of Income Rs.5520x12= Rs.66,240 + 40 % future prospects, Rs.52736 / 1/4 (self Dependency expenditure) = 69552 x 17 (multiplier, looking to the age) =
Rs.11,82,384/- Loss of Rs.1,60,000/- (Rs.40,000 x 4) Consortium Loss of Rs.15,000/-
Estate Funeral Rs.15,000/-
 Expenses  Total Rs.13,72,384/-
9.

Accordingly, the appeal stands partly allowed and the impugned award is modified to the extent indicated herein above subject to following conditions:-
i.
The respondent No.3/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of 90 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against him.
ii. The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court Fee within four weeks, if required in the present case.
Office is also directed to verify the whether any court fees is payable for the enhanced compensation amount or not.
iii. On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
v. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed.
vi. No order as to costs.
vii. The impugned award of the claims tribunal.
is modified to the aforesaid extend and terms and directions as mentioned above.

Therefore, in addition to the award which has already been awarded by the claim tribunal, the appellant is entitled to get the enhanced compensation amount to the tune of Rs.8,09,384/- (Rs.13,72,384 - Rs.5,63,000/-) on various heads.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 7.5% per annum.
Rest of the conditions imposed by the learned Claims tribunal shall remain intact.

v. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed.
vi. No order as to costs.

is modified to the aforesaid extend and terms and directions as mentioned above.
